newsitem.title: USA: Mexico drug profit as high as $15 billion - report.
newsitem.headline: Mexico drug profit as high as $15 billion - report.

text.p: Profits laundered in Mexico from the illegal drug trade are believed to be as high as $15 billion annually, Latin Trade magazine says.
The figure is equivalent to 5 percent of Mexico's gross domestic product.
But if the flow is stopped, the national economy could be seriously destabilised, the Miami-based business monthly said in a special report in its September issue.
The border state of Sonora has become a main shipping centre for cocaine from Bolivia, Peru and Colombia heading into the United States, as well as for home-grown marijuana.

"While the drugs go in one direction, the money from the trade comes back in the other, often in the same false-bottomed containers, yachts and donkey-packs in which the drugs went north," the magazine said.
The money is invested in real estate, the Mexican stock and bond markets, and sometimes public works projects as a favour to corrupt local politicians.

The report said U.S. and Mexican investigators conservatively estimated the profits being laundered through Mexico at $10 billion to $15 billion per year, equivalent to around 3 percent to 5 percent of Mexico's GDP.

"For a developing country which has averaged just 4 per cent GDP growth per annum in the five years prior to the 1995 economic crisis, this flood of money therefore represents the difference between growth and stagnation, or worse, recession at the macro-economic level," the report said.

"This is the Catch 22 of Mexico's fight against the drugs trade: if it were to successfully staunch the flow of laundered money through the Mexican financial system, it could seriously destabilise the economy," it said.

U.S. antidrug agencies estimate that Mexican-based gangs control the movement into the United States of 770 tons (700 tonnes) of cocaine, 5.5 to 6.6 tons (five to six tonnes) of heroin and 7,700 tons (7,000 tonnes) of marijuana annually.
